svg.title: Five Payment Rails Behind the Base Case
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-04-base-payment-rail-yields; chart type: horizontal_bars; title: Five Payment Rails Behind the Base Case; subtitle: Illustrative annual retained revenue contributions sum to $535,000.; chapter number: 2; epistemic tag: illustrative_model; assumptions note: Bars measure annual earned operator dollars, not yield percentages or employer savings. Contract volumes and prices are illustrative. Accounts may overlap across rails, but the same fee cannot be recognized twice.; caption: Revenue mix: $240,000 + $110,000 + $55,000 + $90,000 + $40,000 = $535,000. All commissions are shown after external splits; PBM advisory fees must be distinct from PEPM scope.; stages: label: Self-funded PEPM advisory; value: $240,000 from 1,000 covered employees; numeric value: 240000.0; detail: Charge an illustrative $20 per employee per month across 1,000 covered employees for 12 months. Validate the billing denominator, eligibility roster, service commencement, and termination adjustments in each contract.; label: Stop-loss placement commissions; value: $110,000 from 10 retained commissions; numeric value: 110000.0; detail: Ten annual placements retain $11,000 each after external splits. Disclose direct and indirect compensation, model chargebacks, and exclude the employer's full stop-loss premium from operator revenue.; label: TPA placement commissions; value: $55,000 from 11 retained commissions; numeric value: 55000.0; detail: Eleven TPA arrangements retain $5,000 each under written compensation schedules. Disclose the payer and compensation method; check state administrator rules before performing activities beyond licensed placement and advice.; label: PBM contract advisory; value: $90,000 from six separate mandates; numeric value: 90000.0; detail: Six earned advisory mandates generate $15,000 each for contract reconciliation and repricing work outside PEPM scope. Employer rebates and projected drug savings remain outside the desk's revenue.; label: Workers' comp recovery splits; value: $40,000 from four collected fee shares; numeric value: 40000.0; detail: Four completed corrections each produce a $10,000 fee, illustratively 25% of a $40,000 employer refund. Only the $40,000 aggregate fee share enters operator revenue; $160,000 aggregate refunds do not.

text.title: Five Payment Rails Behind the Base Case
text.tspan: Five Payment Rails Behind the Base Case

rect.title: label: Self-funded PEPM advisory; value: $240,000 from 1,000 covered employees; numeric value: 240000.0; detail: Charge an illustrative $20 per employee per month across 1,000 covered employees for 12 months. Validate the billing denominator, eligibility roster, service commencement, and termination adjustments in each contract.

label: Stop-loss placement commissions; value: $110,000 from 10 retained commissions; numeric value: 110000.0; detail: Ten annual placements retain $11,000 each after external splits. Disclose direct and indirect compensation, model chargebacks, and exclude the employer's full stop-loss premium from operator revenue.

label: TPA placement commissions; value: $55,000 from 11 retained commissions; numeric value: 55000.0; detail: Eleven TPA arrangements retain $5,000 each under written compensation schedules. Disclose the payer and compensation method; check state administrator rules before performing activities beyond licensed placement and advice.

label: PBM contract advisory; value: $90,000 from six separate mandates; numeric value: 90000.0; detail: Six earned advisory mandates generate $15,000 each for contract reconciliation and repricing work outside PEPM scope. Employer rebates and projected drug savings remain outside the desk's revenue.

label: Workers' comp recovery splits; value: $40,000 from four collected fee shares; numeric value: 40000.0; detail: Four completed corrections each produce a $10,000 fee, illustratively 25% of a $40,000 employer refund. Only the $40,000 aggregate fee share enters operator revenue; $160,000 aggregate refunds do not.

text.title: Assumptions: Bars measure annual earned operator dollars, not yield percentages or employer savings. Contract volumes and prices are illustrative. Accounts may overlap across rails, but the same fee cannot be recognized twice.
